Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Insurance Group Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you will need to press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to John Smith, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Insurance Group's Third Quarter 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are David Johnson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; Michael Lee, Chief Underwriting Officer; and Lisa Chen, Chief Investment Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to David Johnson.

David Johnson: Thank you, John, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Apex Insurance Group's performance for the third quarter. We delivered strong results, driven by disciplined underwriting that improved our loss ratios, an effective reinsurance program that stabilized earnings amid catastrophe activity, prudent asset allocation delivering higher yields, solid premium growth from high retention and new business, and our ongoing commitment to shareholder returns through increased dividend payments. Our focus on strategic initiatives like AI-driven underwriting and advanced risk modeling continues to yield positive outcomes, positioning us well in a dynamic market.

Sarah, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, David. Good morning, everyone. As David mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $450 million, or $1.85 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included robust premium growth, favorable loss ratio trends through better frequency control and severity management, strong investment returns from our optimized portfolio, and reliable reinsurance recoveries. Our combined ratio was 93.2%, reflecting effective underwriting and claims management. Investment income for the quarter was $620 million. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with our risk-based capital ratio at 520%.

Let me expand on these areas to give you a comprehensive view of our results. First, I'd like to provide a detailed overview of our investment portfolio's asset allocation, which remains central to our disciplined asset-liability management framework. With $265 billion in invested assets at quarter-end—up 4% year-over-year from positive operating cash flows and reinvestments at elevated yields—our portfolio is structured to generate superior risk-adjusted returns while matching our $180 billion in primarily long-duration life and annuity liabilities.

Breaking it down by major asset classes, fixed income constitutes 72% of the portfolio, or $191 billion, down slightly from 75% a year ago as we shifted tactically toward higher-yielding alternatives. This segment offers the stability and liquidity vital for our property and casualty and group life businesses, where claims can be volatile. The book yield here is now 4.8%, up 110 basis points year-over-year, thanks to the Federal Reserve's rates around 5.25-5.50% and the prevailing inverted yield curve.

Within fixed income, U.S. Treasuries and agency MBS make up 25%, or $48 billion, with an average duration of 6.2 years aligned closely with our annuity obligations. We extended duration opportunistically, adding $2.5 billion in 10-year Treasuries yielding 4.3% during the August market dip. Investment-grade corporates are 35%, or $67 billion, focused on A-rated financials and utilities at 5.2% yields, with an overweight in BBB credits from names like JPMorgan and Wells Fargo for a 50-75 basis point premium over AA without undue spread risk. Structured credit, including ABS and CMBS, is 8%, or $15 billion, in AAA/AA-rated auto loans and commercial mortgages yielding 6.1%, hedged with interest rate swaps against prepayments. High-yield and emerging market debt is capped at 4%, or $8 billion, to manage RBC impacts, with trims in CCC-rated China property exposure redirected to higher-yielding LatAm sovereigns like Brazil's 10-year at 12%.

Geographically, 65% is U.S.-focused for liquidity, 20% in Europe with German Bunds and UK Gilts after ECB hikes, and 15% in Asia-Pacific, including a new $3 billion stake in Japanese government bonds and Australian semis for 4-5% yields amid currency dynamics.

Equities comprise 16%, or $42 billion, up from 14% last year, based on confidence in U.S. large-cap earnings resilience despite tech concentrations. This supports variable annuities and equity-linked cat bonds, aiming for 8-10% long-term returns. Public equities are 12%, or $32 billion, with 70% in S&P 500 via efficient ETFs like VOO equivalents, overweight healthcare like UnitedHealth and Eli Lilly, and consumer staples for a defensive 0.85 beta; Q3 marked a 2% gain versus flat S&P. Convertibles and preferreds are 4%, or $10 billion, at 6.5% yields with upside, mainly from fellow insurers like Prudential and MetLife. We added $1.2 billion in covered call overlays on Russell 2000 options for 150 basis points extra income, stress-tested to 20% drawdowns.

Alternatives are 12%, or $32 billion, our quickest-growing area from 11%, offering 400 basis point illiquidity premiums post-zero interest rates, key for pension transfers and longevity swaps. Private credit and direct lending are 5%, or $13 billion, through Ares and Apollo funds targeting 9-11% net IRRs on floating-rate loans to software and healthcare; we've added $2 billion year-to-date. Real assets, like core real estate and infrastructure, are 4%, or $11 billion, in Sun Belt multifamily via Blackstone vehicles and PGIM-financed solar, with cap rates at 5.2% offset by 3% escalators. Private equity and hedge funds are 3%, or $8 billion, from recent KKR and Blackstone vintages targeting 15% DPI, plus BlackRock evergreen macro strategies returning 7% in Q3.

We've embedded ESG across 40% of assets for EU SFDR compliance in Europe, using our BlackRock Aladdin-powered ALM platform for climate scenarios that cut VaR by 15%. Portfolio duration is 5.8 years against 6.1-year liabilities. For Q4, we anticipate fixed income purchases if 10-year yields fall below 4%, funded by equity sales, plus alternatives from $5 billion in pension inflows. This setup targets 5.5-6% portfolio yield in 2024, fueling 12% EPS growth with recession odds at 35%; our 520% RBC and AA- ratings from S&P and Fitch remain solid.

Next, turning to underwriting discipline, a key pillar is the effectiveness of our reinsurance program. Amid rising catastrophe risks from climate shifts—global insured nat cat losses topped $120 billion in 2023 per Swiss Re—we renewed our program January 1 at attractive rates despite market hardening. We cede about 28% of gross written premiums year-to-date, down from 32%, as retentions rose in non-cat areas thanks to superior modeling.

Performance was exceptional: Q3 recoveries reached $450 million on $620 million gross losses, mainly from Southeast hurricanes like Elara with $1.2 billion industry impact per RMS. That's a 73% recovery rate, beating our 70% goal and aiding a 2.5-point net combined ratio drop to 92.4% in property. Year-to-date recoverables are $1.8 billion with no disputes, backed by top partners: Munich Re at 25%, Swiss Re at 20%, Lloyd's, and Bermuda players like RenaissanceRe.

By layer, our property cat XOL tower has $250 million first-event retention, covering up to $3 billion POP/PA. Elara hit early layers, but $500 million excess recoveries came in 30 days via parametric triggers with Validus Re, limiting net PML to 8% of surplus versus 12% appetite. Casualty quota share at 40% on D&O and cyber offset $180 million in social inflation development, improving net loss ratio 4 points to 64% with 22% sliding commissions. Our new $400 million aggregate cover kicked in after Q2 plan overruns, covering $120 million in floods for a 61.2% calendar net loss ratio.

Regionally, North America (45% of $18 billion GWP) saw 80% cat absorption from wildfires and hurricanes, enabling 95% net retention and 15% premium hikes. Europe (25%) gained from multi-year index-linked weather with Scor SE on Storm Fiona remnants at 65% recovery. Asia-Pacific (18% YoY growth) reinsured 75% of Typhoon Mindy via Toa Re, holding property combined at 90%.

Technically, AIR Touchstone 2024 models integrated with our AI cat aggregator cut tail risks 12%; we issued $300 million cat bonds at 450 bps via ApexCat Re, cheaper than XL, blending ceding costs to 18% versus market 25%. Net retention rose to 72%, lifting property RAROC to 15.2%, 300 bps above peers. With 30% PRI-signatory panel and Etherisc blockchain pilots, we're proactive. For 2025 renewals, expected 5-10% softening per Guy Carpenter lets us reduce dependency while growing cyber and parametrics, backing $1.6-1.8 billion net income and 10% ROE.

Shifting to loss ratio trends, our calendar year loss ratio was 61.2% for the quarter, down 140 basis points from Q3 2023's 62.6% and 80 bps from Q2. Accident year ex-cat was 59.8%, showcasing pricing and underwriting strength. Over five quarters, ex-cat has fallen 480 bps from 64.5% post-COVID peak, via 7% frequency drops and 3.2% severity growth below medical CPI (4.8%) and auto repairs (12.5%).

Frequency declined 9% in personal auto to 72 per 100 car years via ApexDrive telematics, now at 2.8 million users—up 45%—offering 15% credits to safe drivers and non-renewing 8% risks, enhanced by Verisk weather/traffic data. Homeowners frequency held at 4.2%, despite 12% California water claims from infrastructure. Commercial frequency fell 5% to 3.8% per $1M premium on workers' comp ELR controls.

Severity rose 3.2% to $14,200 in auto BI from Florida/Texas litigation and 15% parts inflation per Audatex; our ApexRepair Network at 92% coverage with Caliber Collision yields 18% DRP savings. Medical severity up 4.1% to $28,400, below hospital 6.2%; UK motor flat at £4,200 post-Whiplash, Japan up 5.5% on yen/parts. Cats added 110 points ($450 million pre-tax from Idalia/derecho), 1.15 points YTD; prior year favorable $120 million (25 bps).

Our Google Cloud Vertex AI claims platform automates 65% FNOL, cutting cycles 28% and LAE to 8.2%; fraud detection up 22%, saving $85 million. Rates up 7.2% personal (+11% California), quota share at 2.5:1 for Florida PML $1.2 billion. U.S. ex-cat 60.1% (down 220 bps), Europe 58.4%, APAC 63.2%. Full-year ex-cat guide 60.0-60.5%, Q4 aided by seasonality and cyber pricing.

On premium growth, Q3 net written premiums rose 9.2% YoY from pricing, 92% retention, and commercial wins, atop 11.5% FY2023 versus industry 8%. We guide 8-10% Q4 growth, 7-9% FY2025, balancing rate moderation with cyber/parametric push.

P&C (65%) at 9-11% Q4, 8-10% FY2025; commercial mid-teens on 6-8% rates/D&O cat XL, personal 5-7%. L&H (25%) 6-8% on group/accident. Specialty (10%) 12-15%, cyber 20%+ post-CrowdStrike.

North America (75%) 9-11% Q4 on 7% U.S. hikes, Canada telematics. EMEA (15%) 5-7%, Germany UBI 10%. APAC/LatAm (10%) 8-10% via fintechs.

Pillars: 5-7% rates, 93-94% retention via AI, 12% new biz. Telematics 25% auto cuts losses 200 bps; AI underwriting 40% faster cycles; reinsurance 180% RBC.

De-risking workers' comp for cyber/ESG, ahead of Travelers/Chubb. Headwinds: $1.2B cats, inflation via CCC; insurtech moat via scale.

Finally, on shareholder returns, today we announced a $0.82 per share quarterly dividend, payable August 15 to July 31 record, up 7.7% from $0.76 Q3 2023; TTM $3.24, +8%. Decade CAGR 6.2%, 18-year streak as S&P 500 Dividend Aristocrat. Payout 42% of operating EPS (35-50% target), below Chubb/Travelers 45-55%.

Underwriting at 92.8% combined (110 bps better), $4.2B earned premiums +11%; U.S. P&C loss 64.2% offset cats/priors. Investments +14% to $620M at 4.1% yield, 28% munis/corporates 5.2%. Coverage 2.3x vs. 1.8x median.

U.S. +9.2% auto/homeowners; Europe 15% growth UK/Germany 91% motor; APAC 18% annuities. $1.5B buybacks to 2025 (4-6% yield at 11.2x P/E); $750M cat bonds RBC >550%.

FY growth 7-9% assuming $1.8B cats; 3.4% yield top quartile. This reflects our discipline.

Michael Lee: Thank you, Sarah. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our property and casualty line. We are actively managing our exposure to catastrophe risks and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including advanced AI models and telematics integration that have enhanced frequency control and supported our loss ratio improvements.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. The floor has been opened for questions. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the drivers behind your loss ratio improvement this quarter?

David Johnson: Good morning, Emily. Absolutely. As Sarah detailed, the 140 basis point drop to 61.2% stems from a 9% frequency reduction in auto via our telematics program and moderated 3.2% severity growth, countered by repair networks and AI claims handling. Ex-cat accident year at 59.8% underscores our pricing discipline.

Operator: Our next question comes from Robert Kline with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Robert Kline: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of the higher-for-longer rate environment on your investment strategy?

Sarah Thompson: Good morning, Robert. The elevated rates have been a tailwind, pushing our book yield to 4.8% in fixed income and overall portfolio to 5.5-6% targeted for 2024. We've extended durations selectively in Treasuries and added to alternatives for illiquidity premiums, while maintaining strong liquidity and duration matching to liabilities.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Lisa Patel: What is the expected impact of upcoming Solvency II recalibrations on your underwriting strategy in Europe?

Michael Lee: Good morning, Lisa. Solvency II changes are already factored into our models, with minimal impact given our strong capital position. We've adjusted pricing in motor and liability lines, achieving 10% growth in Germany via UBI, while our reinsurance structure absorbs any capital charges effectively.

Operator: Our next question comes from James Rivera with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

James Rivera: Thanks. On premium guidance, how confident are you in the 7-9% FY2025 range given rate moderation?

Sarah Thompson: High confidence, James. It's backed by 92% retention, AI underwriting efficiencies processing 20% more submissions, and specialty growth like cyber at 20%+. Reinsurance renewals at better terms support retaining more premium while targeting 95% combined ratio.

Operator: Thank you. That concludes the question-and-answer session.

David Johnson: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Apex Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
